newsitem.title: USA: Loose screw blamed for U.S. shuttle's stuck hatch.
newsitem.headline: Loose screw blamed for U.S. shuttle's stuck hatch.

text.p: A loose screw was responsible for the jammed hatch that led to the cancellation of two space walks from the space shuttle Columbia last month, NASA officials said on Wednesday.
A quarter-inch (0.6 cm) screw was found embedded in the teeth of the gear box mechanism that operates the latches of Columbia's airlock hatch, NASA spokeswoman George Diller said.

The small screw, which probably came loose during the vibration of launch, was revealed in an x-ray of the gear box. The discovery was made when engineers gained access to the Columbia's hatch on Monday night, two days after its return to earth.

The hatch, which leads from the airlock to the cargo bay, refused to open on Nov. 28 when a pair of astronauts were supposed to make the first of two space walks to practice space station construction.

The space walks were cancelled when engineers determined it would be impossible for the astronauts to fix the problem. The space walk activities may be added to a future shuttle flight, officials said.
NASA engineers are now discussing whether inspections of the hatches on the three other space shuttles will be necessary.

Shuttle Atlantis, which has five hatches, was moved to the launch pad on Tuesday in readiness for a Jan. 12 blastoff. It is due to dock with Russia's Mir space station to pick up U.S. astronaut John Blaha and drop off his replacement.
